title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten distinct Harvey Mudd and Claremont Colleges study environments, with verified access constraints and concrete features for solo work, group sessions, and computer-based projects.

cards.title: Settle In with a Full Desktop Setup
cards.subtitle: Norman F. Sprague Center, first floor
cards.notes: Bring your HMC credentials to use the Macs or PCs; swipe your ID after hours and choose an available workstation.
cards.short_summary: A round-the-clock HMC computer lab with both macOS and Windows workstations.
cards.evidence_claim: The first-floor Sprague computer lab has seven M1 24-inch iMacs and five Dell Optiplex PCs available first-come, first-served; it is open 24/7 to HMC faculty, students, staff, and emeriti, with ID-card access after hours and HMC credentials required on desktops.
cards.source_title: Computer Labs | Computing and Information Services | Harvey Mudd College
cards.access_notes: Available to HMC faculty, students, staff, and emeriti. Open 24/7; after-hours entry requires an ID-card swipe, and desktop login requires HMC credentials.

cards.title: Work Through Code on a Lab Mac
cards.subtitle: McGregor Computer Science Center, rooms 203–204
cards.notes: Check the schedule at the door before entering, then use a CS account or guest login; save guest files elsewhere before signing out.
cards.short_summary: A 36-Mac teaching lab that also supports homework, projects, and general CS computing.
cards.evidence_claim: The Foo Lab in McGregor 203/204 has 36 Macs for student use and supports homework, projects, and general computing; users may sign in with a CS account or as a guest, subject to the teaching schedule posted at the door.
cards.source_title: CS Computing Resources | Computer Science | Harvey Mudd College
cards.access_notes: Check the teaching schedule posted at the door. A CS department account or guest login may be used; files created under the guest login are deleted at logout.

cards.title: Code Face-to-Face with a Partner
cards.subtitle: McGregor Computer Science Center, room 205
cards.notes: Check the door schedule and use this lab for paired assignments; solo programmers should yield to pairs and move to the Foo Lab.
cards.short_summary: A purpose-built collaborative lab where each computer serves two programmers at once.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pair Programming Lab in McGregor 205 has 26 Intel Mac minis, each configured with two monitors, two keyboards, and two mice so partners can work simultaneously while facing one another.
cards.source_title: CS Computing Resources | Computer Science | Harvey Mudd College
cards.access_notes: The lab hosts classes, particularly CS 70, so check the schedule posted at the door. Students working alone are directed to use the Foo Lab when pairs need this room.

cards.title: Gather a Small Team Around One Table
cards.subtitle: McGregor Computer Science Center, room 339
cards.notes: Email the listed CS department contact to request the room, and plan for a group of roughly ten or fewer.
cards.short_summary: A reservable conference and study room sized for a small project team.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvey Mudd’s CS study-spaces page identifies McGregor 339 as a conference room and study space with an approximate capacity of 10.
cards.source_title: CS Study Spaces | Computer Science | Harvey Mudd College
cards.access_notes: This is among the CS spaces available by reservation, typically for CS Clinic students. Contact the person listed on the official page to request it.

cards.title: Spread Out for Collaborative Work
cards.subtitle: Honnold 2 North, The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Bring your college ID and use the modular seating, pivot-table chairs, or media tables; plug devices into the Power Bar.
cards.short_summary: An open library workspace designed for flexible group configurations and powered devices.
cards.evidence_claim: The Collaborative Commons is an open study area on Honnold 2 North with modular seating, chairs with pivoting tables, media:scape tables, and a Power Bar for charging devices.
cards.access_notes: Harvey Mudd students use their college ID to access the Library. This is an open study area rather than a reservable room; building access follows current Library policies and hours.

cards.title: Read or Review Notes While Walking
cards.subtitle: Bridge between Honnold and Mudd, The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Bring your college ID, cross to the glass bridge, and use a treadmill desk when you want movement and treetop campus views.
cards.short_summary: A visually distinctive connector where treadmill desks add movement to a study session.
cards.evidence_claim: The glass bridge connecting the Honnold and Mudd sides of the Library contains treadmill desks with treetop campus views.
cards.access_notes: Harvey Mudd students use their college ID to access the Library. The desks are in an open library space and are subject to current building access policies and hours.

cards.title: Build Data-Heavy and Visual Projects
cards.subtitle: Mudd 2 South, The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Bring your college ID and choose this open workspace when dual monitors, visualization tools, or specialized software fit the task.
cards.short_summary: A flexible digital-scholarship workspace equipped for computational and visual research.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Scholarship Collaboratory is an open study area on Mudd 2 South with dual monitors, a data-visualization panel, and software suites for digital-scholarship work across The Claremont Colleges.
cards.source_title: Digital Scholarship Collaboratory – The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.access_notes: The space supports students and faculty across all seven Claremont institutions. Harvey Mudd students use their college ID for Library access; consult the space calendar for scheduled activity.

cards.title: Choose a Semi-Private Study Cube
cards.subtitle: Mudd 2 North and South, The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Bring your college ID and take an available cube for individual or group work; no advance reservation is required.
cards.short_summary: Semi-private library enclosures offering separation without a booking step.
cards.evidence_claim: The Library’s Study Cubes are semi-private spaces for individual or group study on Mudd 2 North and South, and the Library states that reservations are not required.
cards.access_notes: No reservation is required. Harvey Mudd students use their college ID to enter the Library, and use remains subject to current building policies and hours.

cards.title: Switch to a Low-Noise Floor
cards.subtitle: Honnold 4 North and South, The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Bring your college ID and head to either side of Honnold’s fourth floor for modular tables and a designated quiet setting.
cards.short_summary: Two fourth-floor zones designed for focused work with minimal noise distraction.
cards.evidence_claim: Honnold 4 North and South contain designated quiet study areas with ample open seating, modular tables, and minimal noise distraction.
cards.access_notes: Harvey Mudd students use their college ID for Library access. These are designated quiet, open study areas governed by current Library hours and building policies.

cards.title: Put a Small Group at the Whiteboard
cards.subtitle: Honnold 4, The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.notes: Reserve with a campus account, then check in as directed; the four-person room includes whiteboards and a short-throw projector.
cards.short_summary: An enclosed four-seat group room combining writable surfaces with projection.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 403 is an enclosed Honnold 4 group-study room with capacity for four, whiteboards, and a short-throw projector.
cards.source_title: Study Room 403 – The Claremont Colleges Library
cards.access_notes: Reservable study rooms are available to current Claremont Colleges students, faculty, and staff. Make a reservation through the Library’s room-booking system and follow its check-in instructions.
